deepLearning.reason: Largest measured target is 123 samples across 35 groups and 2 campaigns. Any neural model would be unidentifiable at this size, and its reported error would be optimistically biased regardless of grouping discipline.

policy.groupingPolicy: Every CV split is grouped by the biological replicate (tray, pillow or experiment). Splitting samples from one replicate across folds is treated as an invalid evaluation, not a methodological choice.
policy.transferPolicy: Held-out-study evaluation is reported for every task where more than one study or campaign exists, even when it is unflattering. A model that beats its baseline within pooled data but fails to transfer is reported as 'experimental', never 'validated'.
policy.promotionRule: A model may only be described as validated if it beats its baseline AND has positive R2 on every held-out study AND its interval coverage is within 5 percentage points of nominal.

existingTasks.reason: Measured per-sample target, but the harvest-mass definition differs between the two arms (documented in DATA_HARMONIZATION.md H1), so the target is not the same quantity across the data. That is why the registry pins this model at 'baseline-only' and never promotes it.

existingTasks.reason: The cleanest measured target in the project (123 leaf samples, 35 pillows, two campaigns), yet still single-crop and two-campaign. Grouped CV beats the baseline inside pooled data; leave-one-experiment-out R2 is negative for both campaigns, so the ABSOLUTE level does not transfer. Phase 7 diagnoses this as an unidentifiable campaign offset rather than a modelling failure and re-scopes the estimand in mizuna-microbial-relative-load-v2.
External (WUR) ground data spanning an environmental grid, validated by nested leave-one-experiment-out. Not NASA data and not flight data; Earth-only domain.

Class-balanced and separable in-sample, but 36 samples cannot support a claim about mechanism, and the labels are environment labels rather than measured plant performance. Useful as a discrimination demonstration only.

ntrsTargets.reason: Seven destructive harvests at seven distinct ages from ONE study. A growth curve can be fitted and its residuals characterised, but the series contains no replicate trays at any single age, so it cannot support a cross-validated predictive model.

16 trays of dry-matter harvest yield from one study, with a documented stress allocation across trays. Tray-level variation can be modelled descriptively; the unit is DRY matter, not fresh weight, so it cannot be converted to the simulator's fresh-weight basis without an assumed water fraction.

Two independent studies report stand water use, but neither reports per-tray or per-plant replicates, and both are confounded by leakage. The numbers bound the simulator's assumed peak water demand; they do not define a response surface.

Peak and cycle-mean rates are printed, and TM-103494 states the whole cycle profile qualitatively (rises to full ground cover, then flat to senescence). No per-day transpiration series is printed anywhere in the recovered corpus, so a temporal response shape cannot be fitted.

A single condensate-versus-added balance, 0.924, over one 74-day cycle in a chamber that leaked 20-40 % of its volume per day. It is the only measured recovery figure recovered and it is reported by the authors as a transpiration proxy, not a closed-loop recovery test. n=1 study.

Peak, cycle-mean and net daily fixation are all printed, plus a qualitative irradiance response. All are stand-level integrated values from two ground studies; there is no per-sample replication, so only bounds and signs are defensible.

Oxygen is never reported as a measured quantity. It appears only in framing statements about what a CELSS must provide. Producing an O2 number would require applying a stoichiometric assumption to the CO2 figures, which converts a measurement into a model output; that is exactly the confusion Phase 7 exists to remove.

The response is printed as a described shape with two anchor points - net CO2 production at 60 umol/m2/s, a compensation point near 190-200, and linear increase to the 750 maximum tested. There is no tabulated response curve and no replicate at any irradiance, so only the sign, the linearity claim and the compensation point are usable.

Two operating points exist (534 umol/m2/s at 20 h and 660 at 24 h in Phase II, 530 at 20 h in Phase IV), and each has a harvest yield. But they come from different system phases with different sealing, nutrient control and, in Phase IV, documented copper deficiency. The two points are therefore confounded with phase, and no photoperiod series exists at constant irradiance. Two confounded points cannot identify a response.

Every recovered report is a ground-based chamber study at 1 g. No microgravity, partial-gravity, clinostat or flight plant-growth measurement exists in the recovered corpus. The simulator's gravity factor therefore remains an assumption and cannot be calibrated.

No radiation dose paired with a plant response was found. 'Radiation' in these reports refers to lamp emission spectra, which is a lighting variable, not a dose. The simulator's radiation-sensitivity coefficients remain unsupported assumptions.

Stress is recorded as a binary per-tray allocation with narrative cause (water stress on trays 1, 2, 4, 8; manganese stress on trays 6 and 7). There is no severity score, no measurement of the stressor, and no control arm. This supports a descriptive grouping label and nothing more; using it as a regression target would be manufacturing a label the source never measured.
